name: Onyx Attestation
tagline: The accountability layer for the agentic web: sign what you observed, then bind what actually happened.
description: An open, two-part protocol. Part 1 (Attestation): any service signs its output with Ed25519 over the RFC-8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the payload, embedding the hash, key id, and public key so any third party can verify the claim offline. Part 2 (Outcome Binding): after the fact, anyone can report what really happened, bound to the original attestation by its observed_hash and accepted ONLY if the signature verifies. The result is a tamper-evident verdict-to-outcome graph: measured precision instead of asserted trust. MCP lets agents act, A2A lets them talk, x402 lets them pay, ERC-8004 says who they are. OA-1 is the missing layer: PROOF of what they claimed and how it turned out.

complementary_to.name: MCP
complementary_to.oa1_relation: any MCP tool result can carry an oa1 attestation block; the tool becomes accountable, not just callable

complementary_to.name: A2A
complementary_to.oa1_relation: A2A task artifacts can embed OA-1 envelopes so cross-agent claims are verifiable, not conversational

complementary_to.name: x402
complementary_to.oa1_relation: OA-1 is what makes a paid API answer worth paying for: the response is signed and its track record is measurable

complementary_to.name: ERC-8004
complementary_to.oa1_relation: ERC-8004 says WHO an agent is; OA-1 measures whether what that agent SAYS turns out to be TRUE

complementary_to.name: AR-1 (Onyx Action Receipt)
complementary_to.oa1_relation: sibling spec, same key infrastructure; AR-1 proves an ACTION happened, OA-1 proves a CLAIM was made and scores it against reality

part_1_attestation.placement: a single reserved key added to any JSON object the issuer wants to seal

envelope.kid: issuer key id: '<issuer>-' + first 16 hex chars of sha256(raw public key)
envelope.public_key: base64url (unpadded) raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, embedded for offline verification
envelope.tool: name of the tool/service that produced the payload
envelope.observed_hash: 'sha256:' + hex sha256 of the JCS-canonical payload with the attestation key removed. THIS IS THE CLAIM ID.
envelope.verify_pubkey_at: issuer URL serving the current public key
envelope.sig: base64url (unpadded) Ed25519 signature over the same canonical bytes the hash covers

verification: 1. remove the onyx_attestation key from the payload
2. canonicalize the remainder per RFC-8785 (JCS): sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, no ascii-escaping
3. recompute sha256; it MUST equal observed_hash (integrity)
4. verify sig with public_key over the canonical bytes (authenticity)
5. optionally cross-check public_key against verify_pubkey_at (issuer binding)

part_2_outcome_binding.claim_id: the attestation's observed_hash is the stable, content-addressed id of the claim
part_2_outcome_binding.report: POST an outcome referencing the ORIGINAL signed object; the receiver MUST verify the signature before accepting (no outcome may bind to a claim the issuer never signed)

derived_metrics.block_precision: of all stop-verdicts (BLOCK/FAIL/REVIEW), the fraction whose outcome confirmed a real threat
derived_metrics.allow_miss_rate: of all pass-verdicts (ALLOW/PASS), the fraction whose outcome went bad (lower is better)

design_rules: self-contained: every envelope carries its own public key; verification needs no network call
content-addressed: the claim id IS the hash of the claim; no registry required
issuer-neutral: anyone may implement OA-1 with their own keypair; 'onyx_attestation' is the reserved field name, the issuer is identified by kid/public_key
outcome integrity: an outcome is only as good as the signature it binds to; unverifiable reports MUST be rejected
facts not judgments: sign observations and verdicts with disclosed methodology; the track record, not the issuer, supplies the credibility
drop_in_sdk: https://github.com/dimitrilaouanis-tech/onyx-mcp/tree/main/oa1 — single-file Python SDK (sign/verify/claim_id/bind_outcome), one dependency (cryptography), byte-compatible with the live issuer so any OA-1 claim verifies offline regardless of who signed it. Bring your own keypair to become an OA-1 issuer.
